description: This figure group is a composite of two tables rendered as images; both panels are typographic tables, not plots, and there are no micrographs, curves, axes or scale bars anywhere in the group. Table 1 ("Chemical composition ranges of the tested Fe–Mn–Al–C grades") has two columns headed "Alloying element" and "Composition (wt%)", with four data rows: Al 9–12, Mn 10–20–30, C 0.4–1, Fe Bal. Table 2 ("Example of hardening effects of discontinuous precipitation") has a two-level header in which "Composition (wt%)" spans one data column and "Hardness [HV]" spans two sub-columns, "Hot-rolled" and "600 °C — Tempered"; its single data row is 9Al-10Mn-1C, with 273 HV hot-rolled and 439 HV after tempering at 600 °C. Together the two tables define the composition space of the tested Fe–Mn–Al–C grades and demonstrate quantitatively that a 600 °C temper raises the hardness of 9Al-10Mn-1C from 273 to 439 HV — the hardening the citing text attributes to discontinuous precipitation producing γ + κ lamellar structures.

subfigures.description: Two-column table titled "Table 1 – Chemical composition ranges of the tested Fe–Mn–Al–C grades." Columns: "Alloying element" and "Composition (wt%)". Rows: Al = 9–12, Mn = 10–20–30, C = 0.4–1, Fe = Bal. No other columns or units are present.

Table whose header has "Composition (wt%)" over one data column and the spanning label "Hardness [HV]" over two sub-columns, "Hot-rolled" and "600 °C — Tempered". One data row only: 9Al-10Mn-1C, hot-rolled = 273, 600 °C tempered = 439.

observations.observation: Table 1 is headed "Alloying element" / "Composition (wt%)" and lists Al 9–12, Mn 10–20–30, C 0.4–1, Fe Bal.

In Table 1 the Mn entry is printed as the three-value string "10–20–30" rather than a two-end range, so the table alone does not resolve whether it means 10, 20 and 30 wt% Mn grades or a single 10–30 wt% range.
Table 2 has a merged header: the column label "Composition (wt%)" for the first column and "Hardness [HV]" spanning two sub-columns labelled "Hot-rolled" and "600 °C — Tempered".
Table 2 contains exactly one data row, composition 9Al-10Mn-1C, with hot-rolled hardness 273 HV and 600 °C tempered hardness 439 HV.
The hardness increase for 9Al-10Mn-1C between the hot-rolled and 600 °C tempered conditions is 166 HV on the printed values (273 → 439 HV).
The caption states that Table 1 gives the chemical composition ranges of the tested Fe–Mn–Al–C grades.
The caption states that Table 2 is an "Example of hardening effects of discontinuous precipitation".
The citing text asserts that discontinuous precipitation occurred in alloys treated at 600 °C for lower Mn contents, enhancing the hardness of the grades.

The citing text asserts that at 9Al-10Mn-0.4C grains underwent only partial discontinuous precipitation, whereas at 9Al-10Mn-1C almost all the austenite volume transformed into a γ + κ lamellar structure.

The citing text identifies the 9Al-10Mn-1C condition at 600 °C as the best microstructure, with carbides from discontinuous precipitation and narrow inter-lamellar spacing, corresponding to the highest hardness value of Table 2.

Neither table reports microstructure, phase fractions or lamellar spacing — those claims in the citing text are supported by other figures, and these two tables carry only composition ranges and two hardness values.
Composition 9Al-10Mn-0.4C, discussed in the citing text, has no hardness entry in Table 2, which lists only 9Al-10Mn-1C.
